- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (positive sentiment > 0.10) — reduce forecast peak values.
- Underestimate prices after strong negative sentiment spikes — adjust downward bias by 2–5% of recent range.
- Overshoot after recent price spikes — cap forecast at 10–15% below prior peak if sentiment is neutral or slightly negative.
- Mean-reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show rising prices with negative sentiment, reduce forecast slope.
- Lagged overreaction: if model forecasts 3–5 days ahead of true price drop, reduce forecast by 1–3% per lag day.
- High sentiment + high volatility = overconfidence — reduce forecast variance by 15–20% for sentiment > 0.20.
- If sentiment is consistently negative and price is trending down, forecast should not exceed 10% above recent low.
